title: Governor of New Mexico

context.text: Open seat: Democratic Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham is term-limited and cannot seek a third consecutive term.

In the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary, former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland defeated Bernalillo County District Attorney Sam Bregman, 72.3% to 27.7%. In the Republican primary, Rio Rancho Mayor Gregg Hull won with 47.0%, ahead of Doug Turner (36.9%) and Duke Rodriguez (16.1%).

New Mexico's lieutenant governor runs jointly with the governor. Democratic lieutenant governor nominee Maggie Toulouse Oliver withdrew on June 18, citing health issues, and the Democratic Party's State Central Committee chose Land Commissioner Stephanie Garcia Richard as the replacement. State Sen. David Gallegos is the Republican nominee.

The Secretary of State's 2026 General Election candidate list shows only the Democratic and Republican tickets as qualified for governor. Four independent filers, including former Las Cruces Mayor Ken Miyagishima, are listed as disqualified; Wikipedia reports that Miyagishima ended his campaign and endorsed Hull.

candidates.name: Deb Haaland
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Stephanie Garcia Richard, New Mexico Commissioner of Public Lands, who replaced primary winner Maggie Toulouse Oliver on the ticket.
candidates.currentRole: Former U.S. Secretary of the Interior (2021–2025)

priorities.text: An 'affordability agenda' within a campaign plan built on education, affordability, health care and public safety, including raising the state minimum wage, a tax-credit calculator and long-term savings accounts for babies born in the state.
Creating a public health care option.
priorities.quote: I want to work toward a public option for people so that nobody is left behind.

priorities.text: Continuing New Mexico's renewable energy build-out, pointing to the 2019 Energy Transition Act.

positions.summary: Her campaign plan includes raising the state minimum wage; NM In Depth describes her proposal as a "living wage" that adjusts with inflation.
Supports creating a state public health care option.
positions.quote: I want to work toward a public option for people so that nobody is left behind.

positions.summary: Praised Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham's work making New Mexico the first state to offer universal, no-cost child care, citing her own experience collecting SNAP benefits.
positions.quote: I often think about how that would have changed my life

positions.summary: Says continued investment in solar, wind and geothermal energy will create jobs and hold down utility costs, and cited the Energy Transition Act's renewable-energy requirements (50% by 2030, 80% by 2040, 100% by 2045).

record.text: As Interior Secretary, announced the Federal Indian Boarding School Initiative, a comprehensive review of federal boarding school policies.

As Interior Secretary, issued a public land order withdrawing federal public lands within a 10-mile radius of Chaco Culture National Historical Park from new oil and gas leasing and mining claims for 20 years, subject to valid existing rights.

candidates.name: Gregg Hull
candidates.ballotNote: Running with state Sen. David Gallegos (R-41).

priorities.text: Phasing out the state tax on eligible personal income over four years through his 'Four Steps to Zero' proposal, with legislative approval.
Public safety: more police presence statewide and a zero-tolerance policy for violent crimes and crimes against children.
Raising educational outcomes by tying a portion of school funding to measurable gains in literacy, math and graduation rates.

positions.summary: Says that as governor he will increase police presence at the local and regional level; notes the Rio Rancho police budget more than doubled during his tenure as mayor.
Says he strongly supports the Second Amendment and opposes new burdens on law-abiding gun owners, favoring enforcement of existing laws.
positions.quote: Avoid policies that place new burdens on citizens who follow the law.

positions.summary: Supports expanding school choice and charter schools.
positions.quote: Responsibly expanding school choice and high-quality charter schools creates opportunity for families while encouraging improvement across the system.

record.text: As mayor, opposed moving Rio Rancho's local elections into the statewide election system, saying it would have removed the city's voter-approved photo-identification requirement.
Reports that the Rio Rancho Police Department budget more than doubled under his leadership as mayor.

researchNotes: The slate was checked against the New Mexico Secretary of State's 2026 General Election Contest/Candidate List (candidate portal): the only qualified governor tickets are Haaland/Garcia Richard (D) and Hull/Gallegos (R); no Libertarian or other minor-party candidate appears, and four independent filers (Pettit, Miyagishima, Kumar, Evans) are marked disqualified. Maggie Toulouse Oliver is listed as withdrawn. Primary results are from Wikipedia's tabulation. Ballotpedia blocked automated access. Running mates (Stephanie Garcia Richard, David Gallegos) are in ballotNote, not separate entries. Hull's mayoral record rests on his own campaign site; no official Rio Rancho city links were found. Haaland's U.S. House sponsored bills were not retrieved. No sourced position on abortion was found for either candidate.
